text:
support: Heads-up — multiple customers hitting 5xx/504s from hosted inference (us-west-2). Spike started ~08:07 UTC. p95 latency > 8s, p99 > 15s for a few tenants. Customer support already escalated a high-priority ticket.

maya_oncall: Copy. Any immediate indicators? queue_depth, batcher backlog, or auth failures?

support: Quick paste from gateway metrics dashboard: `ingress.request_queue_depth` peaked at 128 (configured soft limit 120). `continuous_batcher.backlog` jumped to 980 and stayed high for ~90s. We also see a cascade of early rejects then timeouts.

alex_ml: Oof. Continuous batching backlog ~980 is unusually high. Looks like dequeue throughput couldn't keep up with incoming arrival rate. Any recent model rollouts or config changes to batch size/timeout?

jess_ops: Not that I'm aware of — no rollouts in last 2 hours. Deploy bot shows no successful deploys recently: 
```
deploy-bot: no deploys in last 3h for hosted-runtime/us-west-2
```

sam_prod: Customers report 504s for payloads with long contexts (~12k tokens) and some mid-size requests. Could be that longseqs are dominating batch capacity and causing queue buildup.

maya_oncall: Can we confirm if priority routing or tenant isolation kicked in? If a few long requests filled batch slots, they could block short ones. Check `routing.policy` and `batcher.max_seq_len` per-tenant.

ing_sre: Looking at traces — a cluster of requests from tenant `acme-corp` had KV cache warmups and cold-path decodes. Their avg decode time spiked to ~7s; while other tenants stayed ~200-400ms. Continuous batcher backlog increases when cold-paths spike.

alex_ml: That matches. KV cache spin-up on cold starts plus long sequences -> larger effective batch times. If batch windows expanded, queue depth would ratchet up. Suggest applying temporary mitigations: reduce max_batch_time_ms for that pool, enable request size-based routing to a long-seq pool, or apply tenant throttling.

jess_ops: Short-term mitigation applied: I bumped `request_queue.soft_limit` from 120 -> 160 for us-west-2 to buy time, and enabled emergency tenant throttling for `acme-corp` (10% of baseline). Not ideal but should relieve head-of-line blocking.

support: Noted — informing customers. Any config snippets for rollback/mitigation so docs can include steps?

maya_oncall: Steps I used:
```
# increase soft queue limit (temp)
curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.internal/pools/us-west-2/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY" \
  -d '{"request_queue":{"soft_limit":160}}'

# limit tenant bursts
curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.internal/tenants/acme-corp/rate_limit \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY" \
  -d '{"burst_pct":10}'
```

alex_ml: Also started a canary route: route long-seq (>8k tokens) to smaller, lower-latency model variant. That reduces per-request token cost and helps throughput.

ing_sre: After these changes backlog dropped from 980 -> ~140 in ~45s and p95 latencies are trending down. We still see some 5xx spikes as queued requests time out — need to do clean drain.

jess_ops: Will run a controlled drain: drain queued requests older than 30s with graceful fail + retry header so clients can retry. Command: 
```
# drain old queue items
POST /ops/queue/drain?older_than=30s&grace=true
```

sam_prod: Customer updates: acme-corp accepted temporary throttling; some customers asked for SLA credits — support is collecting impact windows.

support: Filing follow-up ticket for postmortem: need to add guardrails — tenant-level long-seq routing, automated kv-cache pre-warm heuristics, and circuit-breaker for batch windows. Also consider lowering default batch max_time for hosted to reduce head-of-line risk.

maya_oncall: Agreed. Action items:
- ing_sre: dig into root cause of KV spin-ups for acme-corp (job IDs attached).
- alex_ml: propose routing and model-variant policy change + perf tests.
- jess_ops: create runbook steps for queue soft_limit bump and emergency tenant throttle.
- support: compile customer impact and refund/credit recommendations.

support: Thanks — marking this incident as triaged. Will update ticket with mitigation timeline and customers affected. :white_check_mark:
